a high-efficiency CMOS full-wave wireless rectifier has been designed and implemented in a 0. 18 μm standard digital CMOS process.
the rectifier achieves 85.8%, 81.3%, 79.2% measured power efficiency for input powers of 1 mW, 10 mW, and 100 mW, respectively.
we designed, fabricated, and measured a 0.5 mm2 CMOS rectifier with 85.85% power efficiency at 0.2 V and 40.68 Mhz.

the design of efficient CMOS rectifiers for fully integrated wireless power transfer applications.
the design and measurement of high-efficiency CMOS full-wave and half-wave rectifiers for fully integrated m W wireless power transfer applications.
the development of low-power, low-cost, high-efficiency, fully integrated wireless power transfer systems.

the rectifier is a high-efficiency rectifier that is well suited for mm-sized near-field wireless power transfer applications.
the presented rectifier design is the highest power efficiency rectifier design in the 40 MHz frequency range.
this work presents a high efficiency rectifier for fully-integrated mm-sized wireless power transfer systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated a high-efficiency CMOS full-wave wireless rectifier that is suitable for mm-sized near-field wireless power transfer receivers for biomedical implant and lab on-chip applications.
the rectifier achieves a 1.5× higher efficiency than a similar rectifier with a 2.4× lower output voltage.

the rectifier is a high-efficiency, low-voltage CMOS rectifier architecture that is capable of rectifying low-level RF input power to provide output voltage and current to drive low-power loads such as sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a high-frequency rectifier and a feedback mechanism can achieve high power efficiency in a small area.
a high-efficiency rectifier can be designed using a simple full-wave rectifier with a single transistor and an output feedback network.
it is possible to design a rectifier with high efficiency and low output impedance for fully integrated power harvesting systems.
